newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares pare losses, end bourse above 4,000.
newsitem.headline: German shares pare losses, end bourse above 4,000.

text.p: The German DAX index played catch-up to Friday's severe losses on Wall Street and tumbled about four percent in early bourse trade, but pared losses over the session to end well off early lows.
The 30-share DAX ended down 74.26 points at 4,078.60 points. The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer trade, was down 26.01 points at 4,051.58 points.
"I think we have seen the worst for the day," said one Frankfurt dealer. "The selling is not a fresh wave but catching up to what happened on Friday after our bourse close."
The DAX closed over 4,000 points, which traders said provided a valuable psychological boost for the market.

Traders also said Germany's low interest rate environment, even with the threat of the Bundesbank nudging up rates in the near-term, and prospects for higher corporate earnings may prompt the German market to break away from the U.S. market if Wall Street falls to fresh losses.

"We have to remember that the DAX has been a real performer this year and it was time for some sort of a correction," said a Frankfurt dealer, noting the DAX has risen 55 percent since January compared with about 30 percent for the Dow Jones index.
"But the market appears to still be intact and the outlook remains optimistic," he said.
Trading volumes were heavy as top DAX components, including many export-senstive shares that posted hefty gains as the dollar surged over recent weeks, were hit for hefty losses.
Carmaker Volkswagen AG ended bourse trade down seven marks to 1,285 marks, gaining after it reported a 73 percent rise in first-half group net profit and higher global vehicle deliveries.
Banking shares, propped up recently by speculation for a wave of mergers and takeovers, posted among the worst losses, but pared some losses in late trade.
Commerzbank AG, considered a top takeover candidate, was down 2.10 marks at 64 marks and Deutsche Bank AG was down 3.70 marks at 111.10 marks.

BHF Bank, also considered to be a top takeover target, was among the top percentage loss leaders, as was Bankgesellschaft Berlin. BHF fell 1.55 marks to 53.50 marks, while Bankgesellschaft Berlin slumped 3.55 marks to 44.95 marks.
